feature: Operator stock and pallet return customer email/SMS

setup.dependencies: Existing Node, nodemailer, fast-check, c8, ESLint and TypeScript only; no installs or lockfile changes.
setup.git: Preserve existing edits; no commits or resets.
setup.tests: Repository disposable runner, bounded mbbs-tests.slice containers, synthetic credentials and mocked delivery; teardown and artifact removal on all exits.

scenarios: N1: One recipient field on stock/pallet/combined confirmation and return history detects one email address or phone number; US/Canadian 10-digit numbers normalize to +1, international numbers require +country code.

N2: Only saved, non-voided returns with succeeded/manual_linked NetSuite status, transaction ID, and real reference permit sending. Pending, failed, local-only and missing-reference records cannot send.
N3: Server builds the message from the saved batch, preserving exact CMB/CM/RA numbers, deduplicating a shared transaction. No amounts, secrets, client-supplied message or invented reference.
N4: Authenticated operators can notify only their own return in an assigned yard; admin settings require admin authority.

N5: Admin Return settings accept a write-only Telnyx API key and sender number; blank key keeps the old key, explicit removal deletes it. Encryption at rest, restricted files, no key in responses/errors/browser storage.
N6: SMS uses Telnyx HTTPS v2 messages with Bearer authentication; email uses existing SMTP/TLS. Missing configuration produces an actionable error before reserving a send.

N7: Durable batch/reference/recipient deduplication prevents repeated clicks, concurrent requests, combined-return duplicates and refresh retries. Definitive provider refusals allow explicit retry; ambiguous network outcomes never retry automatically.
N8: Provider acceptance is reported as sent to the service, not customer delivery. Failures remain separate from the saved return and never trigger NetSuite posting.
N9: Reject multiple recipients, header injection, malformed phones and oversized input. At most 10 send attempts per batch per day.
N10: Existing return posting and financial data stay unchanged; no live customer messages are sent during development.

failureModel.credentialDisclosure: encrypted persistence, response/error assertions, secret scan
failureModel.wrongCustomerOrReference: ownership/yard HTTP tests and saved-reference tests
failureModel.uncertainProviderResponse: transport timeout/rejection tests and durable uncertain status
failureModel.hostImpact: standard disposable runner and cleanup verification
